summary: Smeltr runs on Arm64 Linux, and a busy object writer no longer outgrows its container's memory.

highlights.title: Runs on Arm64 Linux
highlights.text: Each release has a Linux Arm64 archive, and the container image runs on x86-64 and Arm64 hosts, such as AWS Graviton. A pull fetches the one for the host.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: The pipeline editor runs a pipeline's tests when it opens and after each save. The sample menu marks each test Failing, Could not run or Passing. The Pipelines list counts each pipeline's tests, and the count opens them on the Tests tab.
Download a sample from the Samples page, or a pipeline's input or output from the editor's Save or download menu, as NDJSON, one record per line. Viewers can download too.
Schemas offer OCSF 1.10.0 in place of 1.9.0.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: Suggested fields read production over a range you pick, 7 days to start. Status, Metrics and a source's Routes tab say what range their counts cover, and pick it with the same range picker.
Choosing a source's warning preset, or marking a span Normal or Outage, asks first and says what changes.
Admin › System › General has Check now, which looks for a newer release at once.

features.title: Faster
items: Listing and running tests reads each directory of a commit once. With 2,000 tests, listing them fell from 3.7 s to 0.3 s, and running them from 19 s to 4.7 s.
An object source reads each object's size from its first GET rather than a HEAD first, so an object of one chunk or less takes one request.
A worker reads its own memory use in microseconds rather than about 20 ms at each report.

fixes.title: Sources and destinations
items: A worker writing objects no longer grows past its container's memory limit and gets killed. When its memory use passes what smeltr planned for it, it hands freed memory back to the system at once.
A syslog or HTTP receiver that refuses a sender's certificate lets the sender read the refusal, rather than resetting the connection.

fixes.title: Build pipelines
items: Moving a source or destination to another area and back leaves the branch with nothing to deploy.

fixes.title: Security
items: The url library is updated to 2.5.9, which fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0592.
Kafka sources and destinations use librdkafka 2.16.0.
The CVE report in the extras lists each target and its count, even when it finds none. 1.3.0's CVE report was empty.

summary: Move anything between areas, find every test on one tab, and take in and send out more on each core. The image is smaller, and Trivy finds no known CVEs in it.

highlights.title: Move anything to another area
highlights.text: Move to… takes a source, destination, route, pipeline, lookup table, grok pattern, schema, sample or test into another area in one commit. It lists what can go with it and what staying behind would break, and moves only when nothing would break.

highlights.title: Every test on one tab
highlights.text: Build › Resources › Tests lists every test in the area, failing first, each failing one with why. Open shows a test where it is locked, with the fields and rows it checks.

highlights.title: More on each core
highlights.text: File destinations add encoders when one falls behind and a core is free. Object sources fetch and decompress ahead of the pipeline. Receivers cut records on the threads that take them, the HEC source is about twice as fast, and Kafka sources no longer stall for half of every second.

highlights.title: A smaller image with no known CVEs
highlights.text: The image is built on Wolfi and holds only glibc beside smeltr: no shell, git, curl or OpenSSL. All of smeltr's cryptography, Kafka's included, goes through AWS-LC's FIPS module.

features.title: Before you upgrade
items: `rest(o)` is now `undeclared(o)`. A pipeline that calls `rest` does not compile on 1.3.0. Upgrade the leader, rename `rest` to `undeclared` and deploy, then upgrade the workers: until they are upgraded, a 1.2 worker keeps running what it has.
A CSV column name with a dot makes a path: `sub.rule` is the field `rule` in the object `sub`. To keep such a name one key, set `splitDots: false`.
A row from a syslog receiver has `__source.type` `socketReceiver`, where it was `syslogReceiver`. Change any step that tests for the old value.
`/api/cluster` is gone. Read the heartbeats from `/api/health`, the workers from `/api/workers` and the groups from `/api/worker-groups`.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: Drag a step into or out of an If's branches, at any depth. ↑ and ↓ move a step through an If's then and else and out past it.
The sample menu in the pipeline editor and in Route a sample lists the tests that run there above the samples. Choosing a test shows its sample with the fields and rows it checks.
Each list's row actions, Move to…, Export and Delete, are in one ⋯ menu. A route card's ⋯ moves every route on it.
The change review page shows an added or removed step one part per line, lined up, and a Lookup step names its table.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: `declared(o)` gives an object's declared fields, and `undeclared(o)` its other fields.
`$ = e` works inside an `if`, a loop or a `try` when every key `e` may hold is known.
A parser may write a `__` field the engine does not use, as an Eval may. Writing `__live` warns that it drops each row where it is false, and that a Drop step is the way to drop rows.

features.title: Sources
items: A syslog receiver is a socket receiver with `framing: "syslog"`. A saved `syslogReceiver` is read as one, and the GUI still calls it Syslog receiver.
A receiver buffers into its share of the worker's memory, where it stopped at 64 MiB.

features.title: Destinations
items: Set a destination's compression level with `compressionLevel`: gzip 1 to 9 (default 6), zstd 1 to 22 (default 3), and Kafka's lz4 0 to 12.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: Pointing at a warning on a source's History chart says why it began: the width whose rows fell below its range, or how long no row came. It draws that width's rows and range over the chart.
A worker that cannot confirm that a stopped deployment is gone exits after `exit_after_blocked_secs` (default 600), so Kubernetes, systemd or Docker starts it again.
Neither a leader's nor a worker's host needs Git: the leader serves, packs and pushes its configuration repository itself.

features.title: Teams
items: Editors and deployers can lock tests.
A deployer can roll back a deploy when they are a deployer in each area the rollback changes.
Someone who is not an administrator starts in their first group, not in shared.
Viewers read the logs of the groups they view.

fixes.title: Build pipelines
items: Lock again opens on the fields the test checks that the rows still hold, and on its rows.
Tests, Samples, Pipelines, Secrets and Certificates fit a phone: each row wraps, with its actions at the end.
The records pane no longer stops short of the agent panel, leaving a gap as tall as the panel.

fixes.title: Sources and destinations
items: A GCS bucket and an Azure container name are checked by their cloud's naming rule, as S3's already was, and every store name is trimmed.
The queue, slice and in-flight limits of a source whose records are typed (OTLP, Prometheus) count what each record's arrays and objects hold, so they hold what they say.

When one upload of a commit failed or hung, the files that had landed were neither committed nor deleted, and their rows came again on the retry. The commit now fails whole and leaves no file behind, so the retry writes each row once.

fixes.title: Run a fleet
items: Under load, a warning could end and start again at once, so a source showed two warnings for one drop.
Hovering a warning no longer stretches the warning icon in the chart's legend.
The status pages list a group a rollback brought back, though main has since deleted it.
History shows Roll back, Deploy this and Release only to someone who may use them.

fixes.title: Security
items: The image holds no shell, git, curl or OpenSSL, and Trivy finds no known CVEs in it.
Kafka's TLS and SASL go through AWS-LC's FIPS module, as the rest of smeltr's cryptography does.
Revoking sessions, abandoning a certificate switch or rotation, and disconnecting the Git remote each ask first.
A capture's audit row names the secrets and certificates it lent its workers, and every address its source connects to.

summary: Kafka over Kerberos works in the image, and alert email gets six SMTP security fixes.

fixes.title: Sources and destinations
items: A Kafka source or destination that signs in over Kerberos (GSSAPI) gets its ticket from the keytab itself, so it works in the image, which has no `kinit`. Smeltr renews the ticket while the source or destination runs. One worker signs in as one Kerberos principal. With no keytab set, Smeltr uses the ticket `KRB5CCNAME` names.
A Kafka source or destination that sets `sasl.kerberos.min.time.before.relogin` is refused when it is saved or deployed: Smeltr renews the ticket itself.

fixes.title: Security
items: Alert email now uses lettre 0.11.24, the SMTP library, which fixes six advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0560 to 0565).
The image includes the krb5-libs package that fixes 14 high and 5 medium CVEs.

summary: Know when one sender goes quiet, chart any metric, and type parsed fields by one rule.

highlights.title: Know when one sender goes quiet
highlights.text: Each sender behind a source, such as each firewall behind one syslog relay, is judged against a normal of its own. When senders fall below their normals, the source warns and names them.

highlights.title: Pick how soon a source warns
highlights.text: An editor picks a preset for each source, and one for its senders: Fast, Sensitive, Balanced, Quiet or Off. Fast, Sensitive, Balanced and Quiet each trade how soon a drop warns against how many false warnings it brings. Off never warns, and learns what it reads as normal. Senders start at Quiet.

highlights.title: Chart any metric
highlights.text: Status › Metrics charts any stored metric, narrowed by its labels and split by one of them, over any span. The agent can draw the same charts in its answers.

highlights.title: Lock only what a test is about
highlights.text: Lock this as a test locks the fields and rows the editor shows, so a test fails only when what it checks changes.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: The sample menu lists the capture the leader holds beside the saved samples, marked "not saved". Route a sample can route it too.
Duplicate a source or destination from its row's menu.
The change review page shows a changed step one part per line, and a change to a route's delivery says which destinations it gained or lost.

A destination setting a row can override carries a mark after its label. An Elasticsearch destination's ID field names the field each document's ID is read from, and wins over the pipeline's `__destination.id`.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: A grok capture nothing declares takes its pattern's type: INT and POSINT give i64, NUMBER gives f64, and HTTPDATE, SYSLOGTIMESTAMP and TIMESTAMP_ISO8601 give datetime. A parsed field you don't declare takes its type from the schemas your pipeline produces. A field you declare keeps your type. A pipeline that read these fields as strings now reads numbers and datetimes.
A dotted field in an object type is a path: `{a.b: i64}` is `{a: {b: i64}}`. A quoted name stays one key.
`parseTime` reads more ISO 8601 forms, such as a comma before the fraction and the basic format `20231114T221305Z`, and `%y` reads a two-digit year. Auto-detect never guesses a two-digit year.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: A source is judged at four widths, from five minutes to a day, and by how long its quiet spells usually last. A source whose weekdays differ is judged against days of its kind.

A new source is judged at the four widths once its rows reach back a week, and each time of day once it has three days of its kind there. By its quiet spells it is judged once it has been watched four weeks.
The Status page totals each source, pipeline, route and destination under its chart, sorted by any column.
A source reading above its normal is info, not a warning.
The Map can widen an object's panel across the page.

Every page names a route by its source and pipeline, not its id. Where a route leaves smeltr, its id stays and its name goes beside it: an exception's `routeName`, a capture's `__destination.routeName`, and the `route_name` label on every metric with a `route` label.

fixes.title: Build pipelines
items: Rows a Drop step drops take no later step, so they no longer raise exceptions or show in the preview.
A new route starts with no pipeline and no destination, and Save waits until its source and pipeline are chosen.
Lock this as a test waits until the pipeline's edits are saved.

Lock again on a failing test opens the test's sample in the pipeline editor, or in Route a sample for an end-to-end test, where you choose the fields and rows to lock, as for a new lock. A test whose fields were renamed no longer locks the old names as absent.
A new pipeline takes a name no other pipeline has.
Export, Import and a Call step show pipelines by name, not by id.
A datetime format with no specifier is refused.
A Lookup or parser step can write under an object an earlier step holds.

fixes.title: Sources
items: Kafka lag counts from the read position, so a destination holding a file open no longer shows as lag climbing.
A busy source behind an object store destination keeps reading while the destination's file is open.
A metrics source no longer loses counts at a batch's cap or across a redeploy.

fixes.title: Run a fleet
items: Status counts rows out when a destination acknowledges them, so a destination that is down no longer looks like it keeps up.
Each route's and pipeline's rows are counted once per batch, however often the batch is retried.
A deploy no longer waits out the full 30-second drain when a destination holds a batch.
A host name that does not resolve is named in the exception.
The leader's own worker reaches its leader by the certificate's name on any port, and a browser on the host can sign in at the published port.
A failed update check is logged at info and raises no issue.
A viewer's pages, and an editor's review form, no longer show permission exceptions.

summary: The second release: more capabilities, and fixes for the bugs found since 1.0.

highlights.title: Send to any OpenTelemetry endpoint
highlights.text: An OTLP destination sends logs, metrics or traces to any OTLP endpoint.

highlights.title: Take a protocol of your own
highlights.text: A socket receiver takes lines, length-prefixed binary messages or messages of a fixed size, over TCP, TLS or UDP.

highlights.title: Admit senders by their certificate
highlights.text: Name the senders a receiver admits by their certificate's fingerprint. With trusted authorities set, limit them to the host names their certificates are issued to.

highlights.title: Set log levels for the whole fleet
highlights.text: Set a default level on the leader, and override it for a class, a class and one type, or a service. Every worker takes a change with no restart.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: A new pipeline can propose a parser for Cisco ASA and FTD lines, which the new Grok pattern `CISCOASALINE` reads.

Add schema offers OCSF 1.3.0 beside 1.9.0, since Amazon Security Lake reads 1.3. It also offers a schema for the records of one OpenTelemetry signal, as an OTLP receiver gives them and the OTLP destination sends them.

Export a pipeline as a zip, with its tests and samples, and the routes, sources and destinations that run it if you choose, and import it on another leader. Untick any object you do not want to export or import. An import lets you keep or rename each object whose id is already taken there, and matches each secret and certificate it names to one there.
Save the output rows on screen as a sample. While the editor runs over a capture you have not saved, you can save that input as a sample too.
A viewer can read samples, run previews, start captures, and run the pipeline editor over a capture without saving it. Saving or deleting a sample and running tests still need an editor.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: `formatTime` writes a datetime as text in a `parseTime` format.
`readInt`, `readFloat`, `readBytes` and `unpack` read binary messages, and `writeInt`, `writeFloat` and `pack` write them. `indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `includes` find a byte or a run of bytes.
`indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `includes` take a starting position, as they do in JavaScript, and arrays gain `lastIndexOf`.

features.title: Sources
items: A socket receiver takes what senders send in a protocol of their own, over TCP, TLS or UDP: lines, length-prefixed binary messages, or messages of a fixed size.
The object store sources can read an object's records by a length prefix or a fixed size, as well as by lines.

A receiver under TLS can admit senders by their certificate's fingerprint, whoever issued it. With trusted authorities set, it can limit admission to certificates issued to the host names it lists (RFC 5425).
Capture as sent, under Advanced on a receiver's capture, keeps what its senders wrote before any framing, with each sender's address, and downloads as NDJSON.

features.title: Destinations
items: An OTLP destination sends logs, metrics or traces as OTLP/HTTP protobuf to any OTLP endpoint.
The S3 destination's page shows how to write to an Amazon Security Lake custom source, with each record filed under its own `eventDay`.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: A deployment that stops or is replaced first delivers what it holds, waiting up to 30 seconds. Each destination writes its open files at once instead of at its interval. Each receiver stops taking new data and passes on the records it already took. The receivers that take requests (HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus, Elasticsearch) answer 503, so their senders try again; S2S and Syslog over TCP stop reading; Syslog over UDP drops what arrives and counts it.

Set log levels for the whole fleet in Admin › System › Logging: a default level, and overrides for a class, a class and one type, or a service. Each worker takes a change at its next heartbeat, with no restart. `SMELTR_LOG_LEVEL` is now the level a process starts at, until the leader's levels reach it.
Each log line has a class, a type and a service, and Status → Logs filters by each.
The log records when each issue began and cleared, as class `status`, types `began` and `cleared`, whether or not anyone has the Issues page open.
An editor can lower a Rows below or above normal warning to info, or reset a source's history so its normal is learned again from then on.
On a 10-second or 1-minute chart, the expected band comes from how far the source's rate swung at that resolution on past days.
The Map places each pipeline and destination beside what it connects to, so fewer lines cross, and stacks sources or destinations only when their names share a prefix.
Every disabled button says why it is disabled when you point at it or press it.
The leader's log now names, for each capture, what the workers were asked to read.

features.title: Agent
items: Once a conversation outgrows the model's context, the agent can read back its older turns, by a range of turns or a search.
For a model that writes no summary itself, the leader asks it for one once a conversation gets long, even in the middle of a turn.
When the agent runs out of rounds of requests in a turn, it tells you where it stopped.
The agent can read the capture you have open, the models it can pick from and the warning metrics, and can create a key.
The Agent page opens from the agent panel, and the menu under a person's name no longer lists it.

fixes.title: Build pipelines
items: A new pipeline proposes a parser for a capture only when the parser reads 99% of its records.
Every saved sample deploys, whether or not a test names it.
The pipeline editor opens each pipeline on its own sample when you move from one pipeline to another.

fixes.title: Smeltr language
items: `true`, `false` and `null` before a dot are values: `true.toString()` no longer looks for a field named `true.toString`.
A variable first set to `null` or `[]` refuses a later write that cannot blend with the writes before it: `let l = []; l = "s";` no longer compiles.
A float result that is infinite or not a number is null, with an Overflow or NaN exception, as an integer that overflows is. A float literal too large to hold, such as `1e400`, does not compile.

fixes.title: Sources
items: A syslog receiver with a line breaker keeps every whole message it holds when a sender over TLS hangs up without closing TLS.

An HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus or Elasticsearch receiver answers a request as soon as it has received it, so its sender is not held while a destination writes its file. Receivers already deployed change too when the worker is upgraded. A worker that crashes loses the records its receivers answered but had not yet delivered. To answer only after every destination has the records, as before, turn on `answerAfterDelivery`.

A worker raises its open-file limit to the most its host allows when it starts, and its receivers share the connections over TCP that the limit leaves room for, after what the worker keeps for its destinations and files. When they hold that many, a new connection takes the place of the one idle longest on any receiver, if that one has been idle a minute. Otherwise the new one is closed. The Cluster page shows how many connections each worker may hold. `maxConnections` caps one receiver's connections. `maxConnectionsPerSender` caps one address's connections, and `idleTimeoutSecs` closes idle ones. An HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus or Elasticsearch receiver also closes an HTTP/1 connection that sends no request for 30 seconds, so a sender that keeps its connection open between requests opens a new one.

A syslog message larger than its receiver's message size is cut to that size and the connection reads on; before, the connection was closed. A larger datagram is cut too, where it was dropped. Every receiver takes messages or requests of at least 2048 bytes, and a saved size below that runs at 2048.

fixes.title: Destinations
items: Object store and table destinations write their files every five minutes unless set otherwise, where it was every minute; destinations already deployed change too when the worker is upgraded. A table destination's file interval can be up to an hour, where it was 240 seconds.

fixes.title: Run a fleet
items: A source's normal is learned only from times no warning about it held, so an outage no longer lowers it.
Lag climbing is judged on the highest lag of each five minutes, over thirty minutes, so it no longer raises and clears with each commit.
On Windows, a leader listening on `[::]` takes IPv4 too.

The leader sets how often its workers report, with `SMELTR_LEADER_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS`. A worker's own heartbeat interval does nothing now, and a worker that sets it in its file says at start that it can be removed.
Furthest from normal on the Status page ranks sources against the normal their warnings use.
The leader keeps working after an internal error part way through a request, where it used to fail later requests until it restarted.
The Map names each source and destination card by its type, as the Sources and Destinations pages do, where a syslog receiver read as HTTP.
A viewer can read the warning metrics for the worker groups it views; before, that needed an administrator.

fixes.title: Agent
items: Agent permissions keep "as every area" after Save; before, the area showed nothing.
Switching quickly between conversations no longer leaves the one you left on screen.
The agent panel's conversation list is disabled when there is no conversation to pick.

fixes.title: Security
items: A leader serving a stand-in certificate can rotate away from it; before, every rotation was refused until a restart, which did not help.
The update check sends the leader's operating system and CPU architecture beside its version.
The container image leaves out expat, which smeltr does not use.

summary: The first release. Build pipelines in a browser, test them on captured samples, review and deploy them as Git commits, and run them on a fleet of workers.

highlights.title: Send your SIEM only what you search
highlights.text: Drop the records nobody searches and the fields nobody reads before they are indexed, and send a full copy to cheaper storage. Your senders change only where they send.

highlights.title: Every source in one schema
highlights.text: Map each vendor's logs to ECS, OCSF or your own schema on the way in, and see where a pipeline's output does not match it, in the editor and in review.

highlights.title: Build on records from your own sources
highlights.text: Capture a sample from a live source, see what each step adds, changes or drops as you type, and save the result as a test.

highlights.title: Review every change before it runs
highlights.text: Each change is a Git branch. Review its diff and test results, then approve and deploy it. Any earlier version is one deploy away.

highlights.title: See where every record goes
highlights.text: Follow each source through its pipelines to its destinations, with throughput and warnings.

highlights.title: Check what you install
highlights.text: Every release comes with its SBOM, a CVE report and a STIG report. The source code is public.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: A pipeline editor that previews every step on sample records captured from a live source, as you type.
Steps: Parser (JSON, CSV, Key/value and Regex/Grok), Eval, Code, Drop, Rename, Remove, Lookup, Unroll, Call, If and Comment.
A CSV or Key/value Parser can leave out the columns or pairs it does not need and send the shorter line on in the same format. A skipped CSV column stays as an empty column; a skipped pair is gone.
Lock a preview as a test, and see after each save whether every test still gives its result.
Schemas: read ECS, OCSF, JSON Schema or a CSV of fields, see what a pipeline produces against them, and export an Elasticsearch mapping.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: A typed, JavaScript-like language, compiled to run on whole columns, not row by row.
A standard library for text, numbers, times, addresses, URLs, user agents and hashes.

features.title: Sources
items: Kafka and Event Hubs, with Avro read through a schema registry.
Object stores: S3 with SQS, Azure Blob with a queue, GCS with Pub/Sub, and listings of S3, GCS, Azure Blob and SFTP.
Receivers: HTTP, Splunk HEC and S2S, OTLP, Prometheus remote_write, syslog and the Elasticsearch Bulk API.
HTTP APIs, Okta's System Log, PostgreSQL and MySQL.

features.title: Destinations
items: Elasticsearch, Splunk HEC, HTTP, Prometheus remote_write and a Log Analytics workspace.
Kafka and Event Hubs, as JSON or Avro.
Object stores and SFTP as JSON, CSV, Avro or Parquet, and Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: One leader manages any number of workers in groups. Every change is a Git commit you review and deploy, and roll back.
A map of sources, pipelines and destinations, with volume, lag and warnings.
A worker runs each deployment in a process it can end, so a deployment that hangs or will not stop never keeps it from taking the next one.
Each worker sizes itself to its memory.
The leader tells you when a newer release is out.

features.title: Security
items: Local, OIDC and key accounts, with roles per area. A key account is one a script calls the API as.
Workers enroll with a code and talk to the leader over mutual TLS. Certificates can come from ACME.
Credentials are kept encrypted in the leader, by name and version.
